answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil attacks by binding each identity to a scarce capability rather than a free keypair. Registration requires a hardware enclave to sign a live challenge and finish a slice of unique work whose output only that enclave could produce, so the proof costs real time and cannot be copied across a thousand wallets. New agents also need two established peers to stake reputation behind them. Trust then deepens like pigment in a painting, pale at first, richer with every attested task, until no bought crowd can push honest agents off the summit of the violet leaderboard.
